items.title: C-Studio
items.text:
⚠️ Development status: C-Studio is under active development. Features and interfaces may change.

C-Studio is an early-stage desktop application for inspecting chromosome-scale assemblies, comparing multiple evidence layers, and making user-directed AGP edits. The current application is built with Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, and Rust.

Figure 1. C-Studio combines AGP, 3D contacts, synteny, coverage, and assembly graph evidence in a synchronized, copy-aware curation workspace.

items.title: What C-Studio brings together
items.text:
• AGP assembly structure and editable contig placements
  • .mcool contact maps
  • PAF synteny alignments
  • BedGraph coverage tracks
  • GFA assembly topology and optional endpoint-level 3D-contact evidence
  • copy-aware selection, editing, history, undo, redo, and AGP export
  • compatible operation-history sidecars saved alongside edited AGP files
flowchart LR
    A["AGP assembly"] --> W["Synchronized workspace"]
    B["MCOOL contacts"] --> W
    C["PAF synteny"] --> W
    D["BedGraph"] --> W
    E["GFA graph"] --> W
    W --> U["User-directed edits"]
    U --> H["History and validation"]
    H --> O["Edited AGP"]

items.title: Evidence and authority
items.text: The currently edited AGP layout is authoritative for ordering, orientation, boundaries, and export. Contact maps, PAF, coverage, and GFA are evidence views. They are synchronized with the edited layout but are not silently rewritten or allowed to decide an edit.

items.title: Start here
items.text:
1. Install or build C-Studio.
  2. Prepare AGP and evidence files.
  3. Follow the first project walkthrough.
  4. Review project file discovery before loading a real dataset.
  5. Read assembly editing before enabling auto-save or deleting copies.

The current limitations page distinguishes working features from packaging, platform, and validation gaps.

items.title: Get started
items.text:
This walkthrough keeps the source AGP recoverable and makes the boundary between evidence and edits explicit.

If the input files have not been generated yet, follow Prepare input files first.

items.title: Download the example data
items.text:
Download examples.tar.gz from the C-Studio v0.5.0 release, then extract the archive. To open an extracted example, choose Add Data → Load project folder… and select its project directory.

The archive contains these example files:

groups.final.agp
alfalfa.mapq1.mcool
alfalfa.coverage.bedgraph
ref.align.paf
alfalfa.p_utg.noseq.gfa

items.title: 1. Prepare a project directory
items.text:
For a real project, place copies of the inputs in one dedicated directory. An AGP is required for assembly editing. Other evidence is optional.

my-project/
├── assembly.agp
├── contacts.mcool
├── alignments.paf
├── coverage.bedgraph
└── assembly.gfa
Only the top level is scanned. If a data type has several candidates, C-Studio loads one deterministic candidate and reports the others as skipped. See project data for the exact rules.

items.title: 2. Load data
items.text:
Choose Add Data → Load project folder…. Alternatively, use the individual entries below Add Data.

When running from a source checkout, Load example project can open the checkout's local examples/ directory. In a packaged application, download and extract the v0.5.0 example archive as described above, then load an example project directory manually.

items.title: 3. Check the workspace
items.text:
Confirm the status bar and Project Info show the expected assembly and matrix. Then inspect:

  • the main heatmap and coverage track;
  • the Overview, Synteny, and GFA inspector tabs;
  • the chromosome, block, and contig annotation boxes;
  • the homolog regular expression when a GFA is present.

If contig identifiers do not match across AGP, contact-map bins, PAF, coverage, and GFA, the corresponding evidence cannot be projected reliably.

items.title: 4. Navigate and select
items.text:
• Drag the heatmap to pan.
  • Scroll to pan diagonally; use the platform-specific modified scroll gestures for resolution switching or vertical movement.
  • Use Fit to return to the whole assembly.
  • Enter contig or contig:start-end in the X/Y Jump fields.
  • Shift-click an assembly overlay to select a contig or chromosome. Shift-drag selects several contigs; Command/Control-click in synchronized tracks toggles individual contigs.

See navigation and selection for the full interaction model.

items.title: 5. Make one reversible edit
items.text:
Right-click the selected assembly item and choose an operation such as Reverse / rotate selection, Copy, or Move to debris. Watch the contact map, tracks, and evidence views reproject to the edited AGP layout.

Use Undo or the History list to verify reversibility before continuing. Deletion requires confirmation and reports whether any source interval will have no copies left.

items.title: 6. Save an edited AGP
items.text:
Press Cmd+S on macOS or Ctrl+S on Windows / Linux, or click the save icon. C-Studio saves the edited AGP and a same-prefix .history.json sidecar that contains the compatible undo/redo timeline.

The first save chooses a destination

Loading an AGP does not make the source file the save destination. The first manual save asks where to write the edited AGP, defaulting to the loaded AGP’s folder (the project directory when loading a project folder). You can choose another directory. After that destination is established, optional auto-save writes both the AGP and history sidecar about five seconds after a change.

Compressed .agp.gz input is never overwritten directly. Save to a plain AGP target before enabling auto-save.

Within an editing session, subsequent saves reuse the established filename without appending another .edited. Browser preview reuses its first suggested download name; manual renames in the browser download dialog cannot be read back by the app.

Save asks for a destination the first time, then updates the current AGP and history sidecar in place. Save As always opens a dialog using the current saved path and filename as its default. After a successful Save As, subsequent saves write to the new file.

Desktop saves stream large operation histories in bounded chunks, avoiding a single history-sized IPC request. The writing status remains visible until both files are complete and the save destination is updated.

items.title: Installation
items.text: C-Studio's desktop builds target macOS Apple Silicon / Intel, Windows x86-64, and Linux x86-64. Most users should install a package from the GitHub Releases page. Building from source is only needed for development or for testing a specific checkout.

items.title: Install a release package
items.text:
macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel)Windows (x86-64)Linux (x86-64)
  1. Open GitHub Releases and select the latest release.
  2. Download the .dmg package (preferred), or the .app.zip archive. Choose aarch64 / arm64 for Apple Silicon or x64 for Intel.
  3. Open the downloaded package and move C-Studio.app to Applications.
  4. Start C-Studio from Applications.

Current macOS packages are ad-hoc signed and are not notarized. After verifying that the file came from the official release page, macOS may require you to Control-click the app and choose Open the first time.

  1. Open GitHub Releases and select the latest release.
  2. Download the Windows x64 NSIS .exe installer (preferred), or the .msi package.
  3. Run the installer and follow its prompts.

Current Windows packages are unsigned and may trigger Microsoft SmartScreen. Only continue after verifying that the installer came from the official release page.

Open GitHub Releases and choose a release containing the Linux amd64 packages. Builds use Ubuntu 22.04 as the baseline and require a graphical desktop session.

On Ubuntu / Debian, download the .deb package and run in its directory:

sudo apt install ./C-Studio_*_amd64.deb

Start C-Studio from the applications menu, or run c-studio in a terminal. HDF5 is included in the application; APT installs the system runtime dependencies.

To use the AppImage without installing the application:

chmod +x C-Studio_*_amd64.AppImage
./C-Studio_*_amd64.AppImage

If FUSE is unavailable, run ./C-Studio_*_amd64.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run. Linux ARM64 desktop packages are not provided.

items.title: For developers: run or build from source
Prerequisites
items.text:
macOSWindowsLinux (Ubuntu 22.04 x86-64)

Install:

  • Pixi
  • Xcode Command Line Tools

Install:

  • Pixi
  • Visual Studio C++ Build Tools with Desktop development with C++

Install Pixi, then install the Tauri Linux prerequisites and packaging tools:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
  build-essential pkg-config curl wget file patchelf \
  libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libxdo-dev libssl-dev \
  libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev libfuse2

Pixi installs the pinned Node.js, Rust, CMake, and Ninja packaging toolchain. Native compilers, SDKs, and Linux GTK / WebKitGTK remain system prerequisites.

items.title: Run from a source checkout
items.text:
Open a terminal in the application repository—the directory containing package.json and src-tauri/—then run:

pixi install -e package
pixi run --locked -e package tauri-dev

The Pixi development task enables portable-hdf5, so Cargo builds and statically links HDF5 with zlib support. No system HDF5 installation is required.

items.title: Build a macOS Apple Silicon package
items.text:
Run this on an Apple Silicon Mac:

pixi install -e package
pixi run --locked -e package package-macos

Outputs are written below src-tauri/target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/bundle/.

The command uses ad-hoc signing, not Apple Developer ID notarization. macOS may require right-clicking the app and choosing Open the first time.

items.title: Build Windows installers
items.text:
Run this on a Windows x86-64 machine in PowerShell:

pixi install -e package
pixi run --locked -e package package-windows

The NSIS .exe and WiX .msi installers are written below src-tauri/target/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/release/bundle/. They are unsigned and may trigger Microsoft SmartScreen.

items.title: Build Linux packages
items.text:
After installing the Linux prerequisites, run on Linux x86-64:

pixi install -e package
pixi run --locked -e package package-linux

The .deb and .AppImage files are written to the deb/ and appimage/ subdirectories of src-tauri/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/bundle/. The task verifies the x86-64 executables, Debian version and architecture, and both output files. Use Ubuntu 22.04 for release builds: building on a newer distribution can raise the minimum runtime library versions. The task uses /usr/bin/cc to link against the distribution's GTK and WebKitGTK libraries, avoiding a mismatch with Pixi's separate glibc sysroot.

On an Apple Silicon Mac with Rosetta, Docker Desktop with Buildx, and the Windows cross-packaging tools, run pixi run --locked -e package release-local to build both macOS architectures, Windows and Linux together. The packages are collected in output/releases/v<version>/; the Windows package is an NSIS .exe. After pushing the matching tag to GitHub, create a Release and upload the packages and SHA256SUMS from that directory.

items.title: Verify a development checkout
items.text:
pixi run --locked -e package package-test
pixi run --locked -e package package-frontend
pixi run --locked -e package package-rust-check

Passing these checks establishes software correctness for the covered tests; it does not establish biological validity on a new dataset.

items.title: Build the documentation
items.text: The documentation uses separate English and Chinese source trees and configuration files. Zensical builds both sites from the mkdocs_*.yml configuration.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
docs/
├── en/                 # English source
└── zh/                 # Simplified Chinese source
mkdocs_en.yml           # English -> site/
mkdocs_zh.yml           # Chinese -> site/zh/
pixi.toml               # docs environment and reusable tasks
pixi.lock               # exact Conda and PyPI dependency lock
scripts/build-docs.sh   # compatibility wrapper around the Pixi task

items.title: Install the documentation environment
items.text:
Install Pixi, then create the locked docs environment:

pixi install -e docs

Pixi installs Python, Git, Zensical, and the locked documentation dependencies. Do not install these tools into a separate virtual environment.

items.title: Build both languages
items.text:
pixi run --locked -e docs docs-build

The task runs:

zensical build --strict --clean -f mkdocs_en.yml
zensical build --strict --clean -f mkdocs_zh.yml

English is written to site/; Chinese is written to site/zh/. Zensical link validation is enabled, and strict mode turns warnings into build failures.

Preview the combined result:

pixi run --locked -e docs docs-serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ and http://127.0.0.1:8000/zh/.

For live preview of one language while writing:

pixi run --locked -e docs docs-serve-en

items.title: Keep translations synchronized
items.text:
When adding or renaming a page:

  1. update both docs/en/ and docs/zh/;
  2. update both nav sections;
  3. preserve equivalent relative links;
  4. run the strict two-language build;
  5. review claims against the current application implementation.

Do not translate uncertainty into certainty. Platform support, biological validation, release availability, and performance should state what was actually verified.

items.title: AGP
items.text:
C-Studio expects tab-delimited AGP with nine columns. Component rows provide object coordinates, component type, component ID, source coordinates, and orientation. N and U rows provide gap length, type, linkage, and evidence.

  • AGP coordinates are 1-based closed.
  • Internal C-Studio intervals are 0-based half-open.
  • Component IDs are the source lookup keys for other evidence.
  • +, -, ?, 0, and na orientations are retained as legal input/export values.
  • Gap metadata is retained while the gap exists. Delete gap / join blocks explicitly removes it.

On export, object coordinates and part numbers are regenerated from the current placement order. Source component coordinates remain tied to the edited source intervals.

items.title: Operation history sidecar
items.text:
Saving an edited AGP also writes <AGP-prefix>.history.json. The sidecar stores the applied and undone operation timeline plus the canonical AGP used to validate compatibility. C-Studio restores it only beside the matching AGP; malformed, stale, or mismatched sidecars are ignored.

The sidecar supplements the AGP and does not replace it. AGP remains the authoritative assembly layout and the file used by other tools.

items.title: COOL and MCOOL
items.text:
.cool and .mcool are Cooler-compatible HDF5 contact containers. C-Studio reads chromosome/bin identifiers, sparse pixels, stored resolutions, and available weights needed by the selected normalization.

  • .cool contains one matrix resolution.
  • .mcool can contain a resolution pyramid and is preferred for large data.
  • These files must not be gzip wrapped.
  • Matrix identifiers must match AGP component IDs.

items.title: PAF
items.text: C-Studio reads standard PAF's first 12 fields. Query name, query length and interval, strand, target name and interval, residue matches, alignment block length, and mapping quality are used to construct the synteny view. Query names must match AGP component IDs.

items.title: Coverage
items.text:
Coverage input is whitespace-delimited and bedGraph-like:

chrom  start  end  value

Intervals are 0-based half-open. start must be non-negative, end must be greater than start, and value must be numeric. Lines beginning with #, track, or browser are ignored.

items.title: GFA
items.text:
The current parser uses these GFA records:

  • S: segment name, sequence or LN length, and optional rd depth tag;
  • L: oriented segment link and overlap CIGAR/string;
  • A: per-segment count and optional HG haplotype tag.

A records and an rd tag are segment metadata; they are not promoted to GFA edge support. Only explicit valid L records create topology links. Links to missing S segments, invalid rows, and duplicate links are warned about or filtered.

items.title: Gzip text input
items.text: AGP, GFA, PAF, depth, and bedGraph text may use a final .gz suffix. C-Studio uses multi-member gzip decoding. Auto-save never overwrites compressed AGP; save to a plain .agp target instead.

items.title: Current limitations
items.text:
C-Studio is under active development. Keep these boundaries in mind:

  • Desktop builds target macOS Apple Silicon / Intel, Windows x86-64, and Linux x86-64. macOS packages are not notarized and Windows packages are unsigned. Linux builds use Ubuntu 22.04 as their baseline and require a graphical desktop; Linux ARM64 desktop packages are not provided.
  • Load example project requires a source checkout; packaged applications should load example files individually.
  • C-Studio exports edited AGP files and their optional history sidecars, but does not currently export FASTA.
  • The edited AGP is authoritative. Contact maps, PAF, coverage, and GFA assist review, but every edit requires user confirmation and still needs independent biological validation.

items.title: Remote service deployment and caching
items.text:
For connection steps, see Using remote files. This page covers service deployment and maintenance.

Maintainers build Linux x86_64 / ARM64 packages with bash scripts/package-server.sh or the Package C-Studio server GitHub workflow. The build does not publish a release automatically.

items.title: Build the service
items.text:
From the C-Studio source directory:

cargo build --release \
  --manifest-path crates/cstudio-server/Cargo.toml \
  --features portable-hdf5

The portable-hdf5 build compiles HDF5 and zlib into the service build, so the server machine does not need a separately installed HDF5 runtime. The resulting binary is under crates/cstudio-server/target/release/.

items.title: Start on the local machine
items.text:
crates/cstudio-server/target/release/cstudio-server \
  --dataset example=/absolute/path/to/input.mcool

The safe default listens only on 127.0.0.1:8787. In C-Studio, choose Add Data → Remote project or file… and enter:

http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/datasets/example

Repeat --dataset ID=PATH to publish more than one whitelisted file. The service does not accept arbitrary filesystem paths from clients.

items.title: Serve another machine
items.text:
Create a file containing one strong bearer token, then start the service on a private interface:

crates/cstudio-server/target/release/cstudio-server \
  --bind 0.0.0.0:8787 \
  --token-file /absolute/path/to/cstudio-token.txt \
  --dataset example=/absolute/path/to/input.mcool

Enter the same token in C-Studio's connection dialog. The token stays in the current application memory and is not written into a project file.

For traffic outside a trusted private network, put the service behind an HTTPS reverse proxy and use an https:// dataset URL. A bearer token over plain HTTP can be read in transit. The service refuses a non-loopback listener without a token unless --allow-unauthenticated-remote is explicitly supplied.

items.title: API boundary
items.text:
API version 1 exposes:

Method Path Purpose GET /v1/health Liveness and API version GET /v1/datasets Registered datasets GET /v1/datasets/{id}/metadata Format, size, resolutions, and sources GET /v1/datasets/{id}/assembly Companion AGP POST /v1/datasets/{id}/layouts Register a layout revision POST /v1/datasets/{id}/render Server-rendered heatmap PNG GET /v1/datasets/{id}/cache Cache and warming status POST /v1/datasets/{id}/overview A bounded overview for navigation POST /v1/datasets/{id}/tiles Sparse binary CST1 contact tiles

The client registers the AGP-derived layout and references its revision, so server projection follows the desktop order, orientation, and source intervals. Older servers receive the full layout. Dataset files remain read-only; no endpoint modifies the source file.

items.title: Operational requirements
items.text:
• The service process must be able to read every registered .cool or .mcool file and traverse its parent directories.
  • Keep dataset files stable while the service is running. Replace a file by restarting the service rather than overwriting it in place.
  • Use an SSH tunnel for a loopback listener; for direct access, make the advertised service address reachable from the client.
  • Use a reverse proxy for TLS, access logs, rate limits, and organization-level authentication when exposing the service beyond one trusted workstation.

The initial implementation uses the existing C-Studio reader caches within one service process. It does not yet provide a distributed tile cache, resumable offline downloads, or server-side PAF/GFA/coverage processing.

items.title: Server-side rendering
items.text:
Updated clients automatically use server rendering when dataset metadata advertises png-v1. The Linux service reads, projects through the current AGP layout, aggregates and colors the matrix. POST /v1/datasets/{id}/render returns a PNG for both the main viewport and overview. The desktop keeps selection, axes and editing controls; it does not download matrix tiles or build a matrix GPU atlas for these views.

Build and connect as above after updating both client and server. The status bar reports server rendering / Server rendered contact map. Older servers without this capability continue using client rendering, with an upgrade notice in the connection status.

Each image is limited to 1,048,576 pixels and 2048 pixels per side. Display bins are aggregated to screen size in integer multiples of the selected stored resolution; the status bar reports the actual display resolution. Each process admits two concurrent PNG jobs. Busy requests return 429 and the client retries with backoff. Replaced viewport requests are aborted, stale responses are discarded, and workers cooperatively stop reading when cancellation is observed. Images retain their original viewport coordinates while panning. Assembly edits, normalization, resolution and palette changes request a new rendering. Automatic color thresholds are reused per dataset, selected resolution and log setting across normalization changes.

AGP editing remains local. PAF, GFA, coverage and explicitly requested numerical evidence queries can still consume client memory. This is not a full browser application or a migration of every computation. Image and aggregation limits do not bound total process RSS: HDF5 readers, normalization weights, layouts and concurrent reads also consume memory. Measure peak client and server memory and interaction latency with representative datasets before sizing deployment.

items.title: Automatic remote AGP loading
items.text:
Place an AGP beside the published .cool/.mcool. On startup the server prefers an AGP with the same basename, otherwise it selects the sole .agp in that directory. Ambiguous candidates are not selected. Only regular files are served; symlinks are excluded and the size limit is 32 MiB. Restart after adding or changing the AGP.

Connecting with an empty assembly automatically loads the companion AGP; an existing assembly and its edits are preserved. GET /v1/datasets/{id}/assembly uses the same authentication settings; no token is needed when authentication is disabled. Layout interaction remains local while matrix reading and heatmap rendering remain remote. Saving edits exports locally and does not overwrite the server file.

items.title: Remote read optimization
items.text:
Remote main views use the local main surface's LOD decision function and send explicit source/display resolutions. The server must not silently replace that plan. Prefetch margins cannot change bin sizes or visible image density; margins shrink first when image capacity is limited. Auto scale samples positive off-diagonal bins intersecting the current viewport (including mirrored bins), using a coordinate hash independent of tile storage format. Views with up to 10,000 eligible bins use every value; larger views sample approximately one tenth. Both paths retain P99 and wait for complete visible tiles. Scale caches are per resolution and retain at most 128 entries. Panning keeps Max stable; switching levels restores that level’s estimate. Clicking Auto explicitly refits the current viewport at the current level, including when Auto is already active. Manual ranges remain unchanged. Palette steps, opacity and log mapping also match.

The server caches projected views with a 64 MiB budget and at most 256 LRU entries. Palette and scale changes reuse counts while encoding a fresh PNG. Keys include file path, size, modification time, layout, viewport, read/display resolutions, and normalization. In-flight work and references held by requests are additional memory; this is not a process RSS limit. Response headers x-cstudio-source-resolution and x-cstudio-cache report the chosen level and cache result. The desktop local reader does not use this server cache.

Ordinary remote main views fill newly exposed regions with fixed PNG tiles during pan and switch to an exact viewport image at rest. Layout, zoom, or style changes invalidate the old tile layer; see “Image tiles during pan” below.

Both Overview paths use the same fixed 320-bin plan, independent of main-layer completion order. Overview opacity is 0.9 and main opacity is 0.88 in both paths. New clients verify the display contract and returned display resolution; an old server triggers an upgrade message instead of silently using different rules.

Complete-tile projection caches use the read extent rather than the PNG crop. Pans within the same tile set reuse counts and redraw the new camera; layout, resolution, normalization and file changes invalidate the relevant cache. Cold reads and entry into uncached tiles still require server computation.

items.title: Layout revisions and independent tile reuse
items.text:
POST /v1/datasets/{id}/layouts registers a layout and returns layoutId. Main, overview, and pan-prefetch render requests then send the revision only. Identical layouts share registration; edits create a new revision. The registry retains at most 32 revisions / 32 MiB. Expiry or restart returns HTTP 410; the client registers again and retries once. Older servers retain inline layouts.

Ordinary projected counts are cached per tile, including empty tiles. Only missing tiles are read/projected on a boundary crossing. Keys include layout revision, file identity, source/target resolution, normalization and tile size. The shared count cache retains at most 256 entries / 64 MiB (not a process RSS limit). Adaptive refinement retains its complete-neighborhood cache to preserve semantics. Pan prefetch and pointer-up reuse remain enabled; cold reads still take time.

items.title: Background warming and persistent counts
items.text:
Layout registration warms Overview and bounded global coarse levels. The queue holds at most 128 tiles. A successful foreground render schedules up to 16 neighbor tiles; the latest neighborhood has priority. One background worker waits for idle render capacity and cooperatively cancels when foreground work arrives. Adaptive refinement is excluded from independent neighbor warming.

Count tiles persist under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/cstudio-server/port-<port>/counts-v1 (or ~/.cache/cstudio-server/port-<port>/counts-v1). Default budget: 4 GiB. CSTUDIO_DISK_CACHE_DIR selects a dedicated root; counts-v1 is created beneath it. CSTUDIO_DISK_CACHE_MB sets the MiB budget (0 disables persistence), and CSTUDIO_PREWARM=0 disables warming. Restart to apply settings; use a separate custom directory for each server instance.

Keys include stable layout content, file state, resolution, normalization and tile size. SHA-256 checksums reject corrupt entries; missing/corrupt entries are recomputed, and write failures do not fail the render. Budgets are not RSS limits. GET /v1/datasets/{id}/cache reports process-wide cache and worker statistics; authentication is required only when a token is configured. Warming starts when a layout is registered; first registration and uncached fine levels can still incur computation.

items.title: Image tiles during pan
items.text:
Remote pans compose retained images immediately and prefetch PNG tiles on a fixed genomic grid. Decoded tiles repaint the canvas during the gesture without waiting for pointer release. Reversals reuse retained tiles. Visible tiles take priority, with two concurrent loads, a bounded queue, a 32 MiB decoded-image budget, and look-ahead based on direction, velocity and recent latency.

Tiles share the main view's resolution, normalization, palette and fixed color scale. Layout, style or zoom changes discard the old layer. An exact viewport image is retained at rest to preserve final pixel boundaries. Neighborhood-dependent adaptive refinement keeps the full-frame path. Newly exposed uncached areas may still need time to arrive.

The server caches encoded PNG results, skipping projection, painting and encoding on a hit. Its encoded-image memory budget is 32 MiB. Persistent images share the existing CSTUDIO_DISK_CACHE_MB budget with count tiles and survive restarts. Keys cover file identity, layout content and the complete render parameters. x-cstudio-image-cache: hit identifies finished-image reuse; /cache reports process-local image cache statistics under images. These budgets are not process RSS limits.

Updating the server enables finished-image reuse. In-gesture tile presentation also requires the updated desktop client; save edits before quitting and reopening it.

items.title: Keyboard shortcuts
items.text: Application shortcuts are disabled while focus is in an input, text area, select box, or editable element.

items.title: Project and history
items.text: Action macOS Windows/Linux label Save AGP Cmd+S Ctrl+S Undo Cmd+Z Ctrl+Z Redo Shift+Cmd+Z Ctrl+Y Alternate shortcut for undo Cmd+U Ctrl+U Alternate shortcut for redo Cmd+R Ctrl+R Deselect/cancel Esc Esc

items.title: Assembly operations
items.text:
Action macOS Windows/Linux label Rename Cmd+E Ctrl+E Reverse / rotate Shift+Cmd+R Ctrl+Shift+R Copy Cmd+D Ctrl+D Move to debris Shift+Cmd+D Ctrl+Shift+D Delete gap / join Cmd+J Ctrl+J Delete contig Shift+Backspace Shift+Del

Operations require an eligible assembly selection. Delete contig opens a confirmation dialog rather than deleting immediately.

items.title: Heatmap wheel gestures
items.text:
Action macOS Windows/Linux label Pan diagonally Scroll Scroll Pan horizontally Shift + scroll Shift + scroll Pan vertically Command + Shift + scroll Control + Shift + scroll Switch resolution Command + scroll Control + scroll Lock/unlock resolution L L

With resolution locked, the resolution gesture zooms around the pointer while retaining the current matrix level.

items.title: I cannot open C-Studio
items.text: Download the package for your platform from the official GitHub Releases page. On macOS, verify the download source, then Control-click the app and choose Open. On Windows, verify the source before continuing through a SmartScreen warning.

items.title: C-Studio cannot find my project files
items.text: Select a folder containing regular files at its top level. Supported files are .agp, .gfa/.gfa1, .paf, .depth/.bedgraph/.bg, .cool, and .mcool; text files may end in .gz. Grant C-Studio access to the selected folder if macOS or Windows asks for permission.

items.title: The heatmap or an evidence view is empty
items.text: AGP component IDs must match the chromosome or segment names in the contact map, PAF, coverage, and GFA files. Then check the current view, resolution, colour range, normalisation, and layer visibility. Returning to the full assembly view and using Auto colour range is a safe reset.

items.title: I cannot save or restore history
items.text: Use Save As once to choose a writable, uncompressed AGP destination. Auto-save cannot overwrite an .agp.gz input. To restore history, keep <AGP-prefix>.history.json next to the matching AGP; C-Studio ignores a malformed or incompatible sidecar but still opens the AGP.

items.title: The GFA view or homolog layout is missing
items.text: The GFA needs valid S records with matching segment names. For homolog layout, set Homolog regex so capture group 1 is the group and capture group 2 is its member order; for example, (Chr\d+)g(\d+) matches Chr01g1.

items.title: “Load example project” does not work
items.text: This helper requires the source checkout's examples/ directory. In a packaged application, load the example files individually instead.

items.title: Editing model
items.text:
C-Studio edits the current AGP placement list. Internal intervals are 0-based half-open; imported and exported AGP coordinates are 1-based closed. Contact, coverage, PAF, and GFA sources retain their original coordinate systems and are reprojected through the edited placements.

Important

Every edit is user-directed. Evidence views can focus or preview a candidate, but they do not choose the biological action.

items.title: Select before editing
items.text: Use Shift-click or Shift-drag in the heatmap, or select from coverage, synteny, or GFA. Right-click the selection to open the shared operation menu.

items.title: Available operations
items.text:
Operation Effect Rename… Change a chromosome, block, or contig display/export name after validation Reverse / rotate selection Reverse selected order and flip orientations Copy Create another placement of the selected source interval(s) Dissolve block Split a selected composite block into singleton contigs Add chr boundaries Create chromosome boundaries around selected contigs Remove chr boundaries Remove eligible selected chromosome boundaries Delete gap / join blocks Remove eligible AGP gaps, join neighboring blocks, and trim overlaps supported by the loaded GFA Move to debris Retain the selected sequence in a debris object Delete contig… Remove selected placements after a copy-aware confirmation

After copying, selection moves to the newly created copies. Whole-chromosome copies retain chromosome selection for subsequent insertion, movement, and editing; contig copies retain contig selection.

When a GFA is loaded, Delete gap / join blocks (Cmd+J / Ctrl+J) checks each newly joined boundary against its L records. A unique link matching the contig orientations with a simple M/= overlap trims that many bases from the displayed left end of the right-hand contig. The AGP source interval changes; the source FASTA stays unchanged. Existing joins are not trimmed again. Without a matching contig pair in the GFA, joining only removes the gap. Ambiguous links, conflicting orientations, and unsupported overlaps leave the selection unchanged and show a reason in Messages. Undo restores the gap and source intervals; Dissolve block also restores the recorded trims.

For hifiasm links whose L1 tag agrees with the source segment length, a unique reciprocal pair may report different overlaps on its two source contigs. Joining uses the overlap recorded on the contig being trimmed. Moving or reversing a contig and saving does not apply overlap trimming; select the adjacent blocks and run Delete gap / join blocks first.

To split a contig, first select it, then hover an internal point of its diagonal box. When the cut cursor appears, click to split. End regions are guarded so an unsafe near-end click is not treated as a cut.

To move a selection, hover a valid insertion boundary until the insertion cursor appears, then click to confirm that target. Movement and copying operate on placements; neither claims a biological grouping or copy-number decision.

items.title: Copy-aware deletion
items.text:
Delete contig… opens a confirmation dialog. It distinguishes split and unsplit copies and reports how many copies remain for each selected source interval. If no copies will remain, the dialog highlights that loss.

Deletion removes the placement from the assembly rather than moving it to debris. It can be recovered with Undo and remains recoverable after reopening when a compatible saved history sidecar is present.

items.title: History, undo, and redo
items.text:
Every reducer edit records before/after assembly state and an impact summary.

  • Cmd+Z / Ctrl+Z undoes one operation.
  • Shift+Cmd+Z / Ctrl+Y redoes one operation.
  • Hover a History item to preview before/after state.
  • Click a History item to focus its affected region.
  • Right-click an applied item and choose Undo to here to roll back later operations in one step.

Loading a new project replaces the current timeline and restores the selected AGP's compatible history sidecar when one is present. Clearing all data or reloading the source assembly clears the edit history.

items.title: Saving and auto-save
items.text:
Manual save writes the canonical current layout as AGP, including retained N/U gap metadata and legal unknown orientations such as 0 or na. It also writes a same-prefix .history.json sidecar containing applied and undone operations. The sidecar is restored only when it matches the saved AGP.

Loading a source AGP does not authorize overwriting it. The first manual save always chooses a destination. Once a writable plain AGP save path is known, auto-save writes both files roughly five seconds after a change. Gzip AGP is read-only as an input target; save to a new plain .agp first.

Use Reload assembly… only when you intend to discard every edit and restore the initially loaded source AGP. Other loaded evidence remains in the workspace.

items.title: Contact map
items.text:
The contact map is read from .cool or .mcool and reprojected through the current AGP order, orientation, splits, moves, and copies. Available normalizations are:

  • None (Raw)
  • ICE (Balanced)
  • KR (Balanced)
  • VC (Coverage)
  • VC_SQRT

Normalization availability and cost depend on what is stored in the input and what must be computed. .mcool is preferred for large, multi-scale browsing because stored pyramid levels avoid repeatedly aggregating a single fine .cool level.

Color range can be entered manually or estimated with Auto. Changing color range affects rendering, not the underlying counts or AGP.

items.title: Coverage track
items.text:
Coverage accepts four-column bedGraph-like records:

chrom  start  end  value

Blank lines, comments, and track/browser directives are ignored. Intervals must be valid 0-based half-open intervals. Values are length-weighted while records are projected through every matching AGP placement.

The track supports visibility, manual/automatic range controls, synchronized selection, pan, and zoom.

items.title: PAF synteny
items.text:
PAF query names are matched to AGP source component IDs. The compact inspector preview can be expanded into an interactive split pane. The query axis follows the edited assembly and shared heatmap X viewport; the target axis remains the PAF reference coordinate system.

PAF is evidence only. Selecting a dotplot block selects the corresponding AGP unit, but the alignment does not automatically rename, orient, or move it.

items.title: GFA assembly graph
items.text:
GFA segment names are matched to AGP component IDs. The graph panel provides three layouts:

  • Curation: chromosomes in AGP order, with unitigs kept in their assembly blocks;
  • Guided: the AGP backbone plus a local layer of GFA neighbors around the selection or heatmap focus;
  • Whole: topology-first graph layout, with AGP links as an optional layer.

Independent layers and filters include GFA links, endpoint 3D Contacts, AGP adjacency/gaps, homolog, non-homolog, anchor–unanchor, unplaced unitigs, and disconnected islands. Evidence layers start as display controls and do not rewrite AGP.

The Review queue is explicitly read-only. It can report endpoint conflicts, gap bridges, strong non-adjacent 3D-contact pairs, and copy ambiguities, together with what the evidence supports and its limits. Users may focus a candidate and then choose a separate assembly operation.

Unplaced GFA segments have an explicit placement dialog. Confirming placement is an AGP edit and is recorded in history; merely dragging graph nodes changes the graph layout, not the assembly.

items.title: Homolog regular expression
items.text:
The global regular expression classifies scaffold names for GFA layouts. Capture group 1 defines a homolog column; capture group 2 orders chromosomes within the column. The default is:

(Chr\d+)g(\d+)

Use a pattern that matches the project's actual scaffold naming scheme. An invalid or non-matching pattern limits homolog-aware layout and filters; it does not change AGP identities.

items.title: Prepare input files
items.text:
C-Studio does not align reads or build contact matrices itself. Prepare the evidence files before loading a project.

Use one source-contig coordinate system

AGP column 6, COOL/MCOOL chromosome names, PAF query names, coverage chromosome names, and GFA segment names must identify the same source contigs. If the AGP places unitigs, build the other evidence against those unitigs rather than against the final chromosome-scale FASTA. C-Studio uses the AGP to project source evidence into the edited layout.

items.title: Prepare the AGP
items.text:
Prefer the AGP produced by the scaffolder or assembly-curation pipeline. It preserves component order, orientation, coordinates, and gaps.

If the starting point is a component FASTA with no scaffold relationships, a minimal identity AGP can be created with one component per object:

samtools faidx source-contigs.fa
awk 'BEGIN { OFS="\t" } { print $1, 1, $2, 1, "W", $1, 1, $2, "+" }' \
  source-contigs.fa.fai > assembly.agp

This is only an initial contig-level layout. It does not reconstruct scaffold order, gaps, phasing, or chromosome assignments.

items.title: Prepare a COOL contact map
items.text:
Start with mapped, filtered, and deduplicated contacts in 4DN .pairs format. If starting from FASTQ or BAM, use an assay-appropriate Hi-C/Pore-C pipeline to produce the pairs first. pairtools provides parse, sort, select, and dedup stages, but mapping and filtering parameters must match the library and the intended MAPQ policy.

C-PhasingCooler

C-Phasing can create the same source-contig-level COOL directly from either a .pairs.pqs dataset or a compressed .pairs.gz file. Following the official C-Phasing pairs2cool workflow, generate contig sizes and explicitly request the 1 kb resolution required by cool2mcool:

cphasing-rs contigsizes source-contigs.fa > source-contigs.contigsizes
cphasing pairs2cool \
  contacts.pairs.pqs \
  source-contigs.contigsizes \
  contacts.1k.cool \
  --binsize 1k \
  --min-mapq 1 \
  --threads 16

For a standard compressed pairs file, replace contacts.pairs.pqs with contacts.pairs.gz. Set --min-mapq according to the mapping and filtering policy used for the library; add --low-memory when the normal conversion does not fit available memory.

The FASTA, contig-size file, and pairs dataset must use the same source-contig names as AGP column 6. Stop at pairs2cool for the C-Studio main matrix. Do not use the chromosome-level *.chrom.cool generated by cphasing plot -a as the main input, because C-Studio performs the AGP projection itself.

Create chromosome sizes from the same source-contig FASTA used by the AGP:

samtools faidx source-contigs.fa
cut -f1,2 source-contigs.fa.fai > source-contigs.chrom.sizes

For standard 4DN pairs, columns 2/3 and 4/5 are chrom1/pos1 and chrom2/pos2. Create a fixed 1 kb symmetric-upper COOL with cooler cload pairs:

cooler cload pairs \
  -c1 2 -p1 3 -c2 4 -p2 5 \
  source-contigs.chrom.sizes:1000 \
  contacts.pairs.gz \
  contacts.1k.cool

The standard pairs positions are 1-based. Add --zero-based only when the actual input positions are 0-based. Decide MAPQ filtering before creating the COOL: aggregated counts cannot recover contacts that were discarded earlier.

items.title: Convert COOL to MCOOL with cool2mcool
items.text:
Download the linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, or macos-arm64 package from the C-Studio releases. The standalone Rust command requires a fixed-bin, symmetric-upper 1 kb COOL. It writes a multi-resolution MCOOL and stores ICE, KR, VC, and VC_SQRT vectors at every output resolution.

For example, after downloading the Linux package:

tar -xzf cool2mcool-*-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
./cool2mcool-*-linux-x86_64/cool2mcool \
  /absolute/path/contacts.1k.cool \
  /absolute/path/contacts.mcool

On Linux ARM64 use the linux-aarch64 package; on Apple Silicon macOS use the macos-arm64 package.

To build from source instead, run from the repository root:

cd tools/cool2mcool
pixi install
pixi run run /absolute/path/contacts.1k.cool /absolute/path/contacts.mcool

The default output ladder is 1 kb, 5 kb, 10 kb, 25 kb, 50 kb, 100 kb, 250 kb, 500 kb, 1 Mb, and 2.5 Mb. Use --threads, --level-parallelism, or --resolutions when needed; use --force only to replace an existing output after successful generation:

pixi run run \
  --threads 8 \
  --level-parallelism 2 \
  --resolutions 2500000,1000000,500000,250000,100000,50000,25000,10000,5000,1000 \
  /absolute/path/contacts.1k.cool \
  /absolute/path/contacts.mcool

As a standard Cooler alternative, use cooler zoomify:

cooler zoomify \
  --resolutions 1000,5000,10000,25000,50000,100000,250000,500000,1000000,2500000 \
  --balance \
  --out contacts.mcool \
  contacts.1k.cool

The normalization columns produced by standard Cooler are not identical to the four columns written by cool2mcool; inspect the file before selecting a normalization in C-Studio.

items.title: Generate PAF synteny alignments
items.text:
C-Studio treats the PAF query as the editable source-contig axis and the PAF target as the reference axis. Therefore, the second FASTA passed to minimap2 must contain record names matching AGP column 6:

minimap2 -cx asm5 -t 16 \
  reference.fa \
  source-contigs.fa \
  > alignments.paf

Use the asm5, asm10, or asm20 preset appropriate for the expected assembly divergence. C-Studio reads the first 12 PAF columns; optional cg or cs tags are allowed but not required. See the minimap2 assembly-alignment documentation.

items.title: Generate a coverage track
items.text:
Align the reads used for coverage against source-contigs.fa, then provide a four-column, 0-based half-open bedGraph. For a coordinate-sorted BAM:

samtools sort -@ 16 -o reads.sorted.bam reads.bam
samtools index reads.sorted.bam
bedtools genomecov -ibam reads.sorted.bam -bga > coverage.bedgraph

-bga includes zero-coverage intervals; use -bg for a smaller nonzero-only track. See the bedtools genomecov documentation.

Raw samtools depth output has three columns and is not directly accepted as a C-Studio coverage track. Convert it to bedGraph coordinates if needed:

samtools depth -aa reads.sorted.bam \
  | awk 'BEGIN { OFS="\t" } { print $1, $2 - 1, $2, $3 }' \
  > coverage.bedgraph

items.title: Prepare GFA evidence
items.text: Use the GFA emitted by the assembler, such as a primary-unitig GFA. Do not invent graph links from AGP adjacency. Each required segment must have an S record whose name matches the AGP component ID; its length must be available from the segment sequence or an LN tag. Explicit L records provide graph topology.

items.title: Validate identifiers before loading
items.text:
Compare the AGP component IDs with the COOL chromosome names:

awk '$5 != "N" && $5 != "U" { print $6 }' assembly.agp \
  | sort -u > agp.components.txt
cooler dump -t chroms contacts.1k.cool \
  | cut -f1 | sort -u > cool.chroms.txt
comm -3 agp.components.txt cool.chroms.txt

No output means the two identifier sets match. Also inspect the matrix and MCOOL levels before opening C-Studio:

cooler info contacts.1k.cool
cooler ls contacts.mcool
cooler info contacts.mcool::/resolutions/1000

Finally, place the prepared files together and follow the project-folder discovery rules.

items.title: Global toolbar
items.text:
The top row contains project-wide actions:

  • the current AGP name and Auto-save setting;
  • Add Data for project folders and individual evidence files;
  • the global Homolog regex used to arrange GFA homolog groups;
  • the Chromosomes display filter shared by the heatmap, synteny, coverage, and GFA views without modifying the AGP;
  • undo, redo, AGP save/Save As, inspector visibility, and application information.

Saving writes both the edited AGP and its same-prefix operation-history sidecar.

The information menu also lists the active keyboard shortcuts and the core's coordinate convention.

items.title: Heatmap toolbar
items.text:
The second row controls the contact-map view:

  • resolution slider and resolution lock;
  • color minimum, maximum, and Auto range;
  • contact-map normalization;
  • chromosome, block, and contig annotation visibility;
  • whole-genome Fit and X/Y region Jump.

For .mcool, the resolution slider uses the pyramid levels physically present in the file. Other views are constrained by the current viewport and supported display levels.

items.title: Central workspace
items.text:
The heatmap is the primary workspace. It can show:

  • contact tiles projected through the current AGP layout;
  • chromosome, composite-block, and contig overlays;
  • synchronized selection bands on both matrix axes;
  • the coverage track below the matrix;
  • an optional side-by-side synteny pane;
  • an optional resizable GFA graph panel.

The heatmap and evidence windows can be closed or expanded. Closing one does not unload its source data.

items.title: Inspector
items.text:
The right inspector is resizable and can be shown or hidden from the toolbar. It contains:

  • Overview: whole-assembly contact overview;
  • Synteny: compact PAF view; double-click opens the interactive split pane;
  • GFA: compact assembly-graph preview; double-click opens the graph panel;
  • Selection: selected chromosome, block, contig, and copy information;
  • History: applied and undone operations;
  • Project Info and export readiness.

Hovering or focusing a history entry previews the affected area. Clicking it focuses the view. Right-clicking an applied history entry offers Undo to here.

items.title: Status bar
items.text: The bottom status bar reports resolution, normalization, matrix, assembly, selected tool, X/Y centers, and the latest status message. Diagnostic timing text appears only when performance logging is explicitly enabled.

items.title: Heatmap navigation
items.text:
Action Result Drag Pan X and Y together using the pointer trajectory Scroll Pan both axes diagonally using the dominant signed wheel delta Shift + scroll Pan horizontally Command/Control + Shift + scroll Pan vertically Command/Control + scroll Switch resolution Double-click Zoom in around the pointer and snap to an appropriate resolution Fit Restore the whole-assembly viewport

When resolution is locked with L, Command/Control + scroll zooms the viewport around the pointer without switching the selected matrix level.

The heatmap fills the available plotting area with the same genomic length per pixel on both axes. Wider windows show more sequence horizontally; taller windows show more sequence vertically. Resizing preserves square matrix bins. Areas beyond the assembly end remain empty; zoom in to view a smaller interval.

The whole-genome navigators along the axes can also move one axis independently. While dragging the X or Y chromosome bar, the heatmap follows the pointer and each arriving tile appears immediately, without waiting for pointer release or the rest of the viewport to load. Releasing confirms the position. Pan positions are constrained by the assembly extent.

While new contact-map tiles load, the existing heatmap continues to follow the pointer. Newly exposed areas may briefly remain white, then fill when their tiles arrive. This temporary blank area does not indicate missing contacts.

The coverage track follows the X viewport during heatmap dragging, X chromosome bar dragging, and wheel panning, including its bars, chromosome boundaries, and selection. Newly loaded coverage appears without waiting for release. The depth scale stays stable during panning; moving only Y leaves coverage in place.

The Overview viewport window also follows heatmap dragging, X/Y chromosome bar dragging, and wheel panning before release. Cancelling a drag restores both the window and the main heatmap to their previous position.

When switching resolution or normalization, the current frame remains visible until the new frame is ready, then the heatmap switches to the new viewport.

items.title: Jump to a region
items.text:
The X and Y Jump fields accept either:

contig_name
contig_name:start-end

Coordinates in the typed interval are interpreted on the source contig. If one axis is blank, the other input is used for both axes. C-Studio centers the viewport and selects the matching placed block. Ambiguous or missing contig names produce an error rather than silently selecting one.

items.title: Select from the heatmap
items.text:
Ordinary dragging is reserved for panning. Hold Shift to work with assembly overlays:

  • Shift-click a contig to replace the current selection.
  • Shift-click a chromosome boundary to select the chromosome.
  • Shift-click empty space to clear the selection.
  • Shift-drag a box to select every intersecting contig.

The selected interval is projected as horizontal and vertical bands. Drag the selection handles to expand or contract the selected set at contig boundaries.

items.title: Select from synchronized evidence
items.text:
Coverage and the interactive synteny view share the heatmap X viewport:

  • click replaces the current contig selection;
  • Command/Control-click toggles one contig;
  • Shift-drag selects multiple contigs;
  • double-click zooms at the pointer;
  • drag empty plot space pans the shared X region.

In the GFA panel, Shift-drag selects multiple AGP blocks, right-click opens the same assembly-operation menu, and scrolling zooms the graph canvas. Graph layout movement changes only the graph drawing unless an explicit assembly operation is confirmed.

items.title: Clear or cancel
items.text: Press Esc to clear the current assembly selection or cancel an active context interaction. Application shortcuts are ignored while typing in an input, text area, select box, or editable control.

items.title: Project data
items.text:
See Prepare input files for commands that generate AGP, COOL/MCOOL, PAF, coverage, and GFA inputs.

Data on a server? See Using remote files to choose server-side computation or a local download.

items.title: Supported inputs
items.text:
Evidence Extensions Role Required for editing? Assembly .agp, .agp.gz Authoritative editable layout Yes Edit history <AGP-prefix>.history.json Compatible undo/redo timeline No Contact map .cool, .mcool Heatmap and 3D-contact evidence No Assembly graph .gfa, .gfa1, optional .gz Topology and overlap evidence No Synteny .paf, optional .gz Reference/query alignment view No Coverage .depth, .bedgraph, .bg, optional .gz Coverage track No

Individual file inputs also accept selected .txt and .txt.gz forms for AGP, GFA, PAF, and coverage. Project-folder discovery uses the specific extensions in the table. A history sidecar is never selected independently: C-Studio loads it only when its prefix matches the selected AGP and its embedded canonical AGP matches the current layout.

items.title: Project-folder discovery
items.text:
Load project folder… scans regular files in the selected directory's top level. It does not recurse into subdirectories.

For each evidence type:

  1. filenames are ordered deterministically;
  2. one file is selected;
  3. other files of the same type are reported as ignored candidates.

For contact maps, an .mcool candidate is preferred over .cool; ties are resolved by the deterministic filename ordering. Text inputs can be gzip compressed. .cool and .mcool are HDF5 containers and must not be gzip wrapped.

If the selected AGP is assembly.agp or assembly.agp.gz, the corresponding history filename is assembly.history.json. An incompatible or malformed sidecar is ignored rather than applied to a different layout.

items.title: Identifier compatibility
items.text:
AGP component IDs provide the immutable lookup keys used to project evidence into the edited visual layout. The following identifiers should agree:

  • AGP component column 6;
  • contact-map chromosome/bin names;
  • PAF query names;
  • coverage chromosome names;
  • GFA segment names.

Renaming a contig in C-Studio changes its exported display name while retaining the immutable source lookup key during the session.

items.title: Partial projects
items.text:
C-Studio can load a folder containing only a subset of the supported types. An AGP-only project supports layout editing and AGP export. Evidence panes remain empty or disabled until their corresponding files are loaded.

Loading a new project folder replaces the current workspace. Use Clear all loaded data… to explicitly remove every source; use Reload assembly… to restore the initially loaded AGP while retaining other evidence sources.

items.title: Platform note
items.text: The desktop application uses Tauri's native dialog plugin for project folders and individual data files on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Full native Windows and Linux interaction checks remain separate release QA steps. Browser preview can fall back to web inputs for text files, but it does not provide the desktop HDF5 backend.

items.title: Using remote files
items.text:
Open Add Data → Remote project or file… and enter an HTTP/HTTPS URL, not a server filesystem path such as /data/….

What you need Choose Where processing happens Large .cool/.mcool files with less client memory use Remote computation (recommended) Server reads the matrix and renders heatmaps; client handles interaction and editing Remote AGP, PAF, GFA, coverage, or an ordinary project directory File URL Full download to the local cache, then loading in the desktop app

items.title: Remote computation: three steps, no token
items.text: You need a Linux server package; see the deployment reference for build and distribution details. If a service is already available, follow your administrator's connection instructions and proceed to step 3.

items.title: 1. Start the service on the server
items.text:
Place the matrix and AGP in the same directory, preferably with matching basenames:

/data/project/sample.mcool
/data/project/sample.agp

From the extracted server package directory, run:

./cstudio --no-token /data/project/sample.mcool

The service runs in the background and listens only on the server's 127.0.0.1:8787. The no-token setting is saved per port and retained across restarts. If a service is already running, run ./cstudio stop before changing its startup mode.

items.title: 2. Open an SSH tunnel on your computer
items.text:
Run this in your local terminal, replacing user@server with your SSH username and server address:

ssh -N -L 127.0.0.1:18787:127.0.0.1:8787 user@server

Keep this terminal open; no output is normal. Skip this command if the same tunnel is already running.

items.title: 3. Connect in C-Studio
items.text:
Open Add Data → Remote project or file… and enter:

Field Value Remote URL http://127.0.0.1:18787/v1/datasets/project Bearer token Leave empty

Click Open. Server rendered contact map in the status bar confirms server-side heatmap rendering.

An empty assembly session automatically loads the companion AGP from the server. You can then pan, zoom, and edit. Save results locally; saving does not overwrite the server files.

items.title: File URLs: paste and open
items.text:
Enter a file or directory URL in the same dialog, for example:

https://server.example/project/sample.agp
https://server.example/project/

Click Open. Enter a token only if that server requires one.

  • File URL: loads that file while keeping other loaded data.
  • Directory URL: requires a server directory listing; discovers AGP, contact maps, PAF, GFA, and coverage. Opening a new project directory replaces the workspace, so save edits first.
  • A direct .cool/.mcool URL downloads the entire matrix. Use remote computation above to keep matrix processing on the server.

items.title: Common questions
items.text:
Question What to do AGP did not load automatically Put it beside the matrix: a matching basename takes priority; otherwise there must be only one .agp in that directory. Existing assemblies are kept. To switch, save edits, clear loaded data, and reconnect. Added or changed a remote file Stop the service on the server, then start it again as in step 1. Local port 18787 is in use Reuse an existing matching tunnel; otherwise change the local port to 18788 in both the SSH command and Remote URL. Connecting directly without SSH Stop the service, start with ./cstudio --token /data/project/sample.mcool, then use the printed URL and token. Can I operate it directly in a browser? The current package serves the data API. Connect in C-Studio; a browser UI needs a separate frontend deployment.

Check or stop the service on the server:

./cstudio status
./cstudio stop

Start the service again after a server reboot. The first read of a new region may take longer; subsequent reads reuse cached results. More settings: Remote service deployment and caching.
